questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic level primarily, and the fact that I was able to speak the language ahead of time. I also wanted to explore the US and get a feel for high level learning.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought all my courses were great - Applied Complex Analysis, Measure Theory and Lebesgue integration, Quantum Information Processing, Computational Physics. I also highly recommend taking Introduction to Wines as it was a great way to get know some of the other exchange students, and it was super interesting to learn about the world of wine. I met some great friends, the campus and surrounding areas were extremely beautiful and it was a super super good exchange stay.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Mostly easy, the incoming exchange advisors had set up info in a logical and manageable way which was very nice. Housing was the only thing I had some nervousness with, but the process turned out just OK, the advisors were good at letting us know about housing opportunities.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance with the orientation session, which was fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The process was fine, I recommend taking the opportunities given by the incoming exchange advisors at Cornell, and searching Facebook and the like for any sublets (but being aware of scammers). And also contacting local landlords, and finding out if other students from Copenhagen are going to the same place, as finding larger places seems to be easier.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets are quite far away, so I would recommend a shopping delivery service like Instacart. Or getting the on-campus meal plan, or staying in a co-op or frat house, which usually have in-house cooking.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration through the Student Center was straightforward, if you have researched the courses you want to follow while attending.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I believe the incoming exchange advisors were very happy to help, but I did not feel I needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% successful, the demand for standard physics and math courses was not very high. Economics and computer science seemed a bit tougher.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the proces and know which courses seem interesting, and have backup courses. And also feel free to switch courses in the add period, if the course or instructor is not good.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three 4000 and one 6000 level course, the level was very manageable I think, and I think 3000 and up is a good fit for the academic level I am used to in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: For me, it was a lot more self-studying than I am used to, there were no tutorials in my classes, or discussions. In some classes there were discussions, but most problem sets were to be solved on your own, without any help. I find that I learn much more when I have a TA to ask questions, but this way of teaching worked fine for me too.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Applied Complex Analysis
Computational Physics 
Quantum Information Processing
Measure Theory and Lebesgue Integration
Introduction to Wines

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Introduction to Wines was very fun and a great way to meet other people. I would also recommend Applied Complex Analysis for the lectures with professor Steven Strogatz, who is very good at communicating. If you are up for a challenge that is also very rewarding, I found Quantum Information Processing to be quite difficult but also very satisfying.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The mandatory health insurance was about $1700 which was a little unexpected, but good to have in the US I think. I also went on some trips that I did not plan ahead, but were still very much worth it. Also tipping and sales tax on all good are a constant unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are about the same as in Denmark, so a little expensive. Housing is also quite expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Football (soccer), debating, chess, tennis, badminton, climbing. Pretty much any sport you could think of. Also consulting clubs and entrepreneurial clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Climbing with other was super fun, I found.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the surrounding areas and see the gorges, Second Dam, Ludlowville Falls, Taughannock Falls. Also for longer trips, go to Canada or New York City.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Mostly easy, the cultures are quite similar. Although americans are very chatty and upbeat, which was nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say yes to any activities that others suggest, at least in the beginning during the first few weeks. After that I found it was very easy to have a group to hang around with. And say hi when you see someone you have seen before and so on.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything particularly challenging I think.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness to talking to anyone, even if you don't know them. And the culture of excelling, there is very much room for you to pursue your passions.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get to know the other exchange students by talking to anyone you see, and going along with activities.
Take the wines class.
See the surrounding nature.
And just enjoy the whole experience, it is really really great!!!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Can't think of anything no.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Making friends with people from all around the world, as well as taking courses at a high-level US university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Also meeting people, but the challenge was quickly overcome I felt.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Please go, Cornell was fantastic!!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
